66728-the-kingmakers.description: A book by Burton E. Stevenson. It was the women who dominated the scene. arxiv-2103-06703.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Joseph D. Osborn, Anthony D. Frawley, Jin Huang, Sookhyun Lee, Hugo Pereira Da Costa, Michael Peters, Chris Pinkenburg, Christof Roland, Haiwang Yu. sPHENIX is a high energy nuclear physics experiment under construction at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider at Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL).

arxiv-2208-14296.title: Features of Molecular Structure Beneficial for Optical Pumping
arxiv-2208-14296.creator: James B. Dragan, Ivan O. Antonov, Brian C. Odom
arxiv-2208-14296.description: Abstract Fast and efficient state preparation of molecules can be accomplished by optical pumping. Molecular structure that most obviously facilitates cycling involves a strong electronic transition, with favorable vibrational branching (diagonal Franck-Condon factors, aka FCFs) and without any intervening electronic states. Here, we propose important adjustments to those criteria, based on our experience optically pumping SiO + .

arxiv-2402-10403.title: Polyhedral Complex Derivation from Piecewise Trilinear Networks
arxiv-2402-10403.creator: Jin-Hwa Kim
arxiv-2402-10403.description: Abstract Recent advancements in visualizing deep neural networks provide insights into their structures and mesh extraction from Continuous Piecewise Affine (CPWA) functions. Meanwhile, developments in neural surface representation learning incorporate non-linear positional encoding, addressing issues like spectral bias; however, this poses challenges in applying mesh extraction techniques based on CPWA functions.

arxiv-2407-13551.title: Decoding the interaction mediators from landscape-induced spatial patterns
arxiv-2407-13551.creator: E. H. Colombo, L. Defaveri, C. Anteneodo
arxiv-2407-13551.description: Abstract Interactions between organisms are mediated by an intricate network of physico-chemical substances and other organisms. Understanding the dynamics of mediators and how they shape the population spatial distribution is key to predict ecological outcomes and how they would be transformed by changes in environmental constraints.

arxiv-2410-09163.title: Learning to Walk from Three Minutes of Real-World Data with Semi-structured Dynamics Models
arxiv-2410-09163.creator: Jacob Levy, Tyler Westenbroek, David Fridovich-Keil
arxiv-2410-09163.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jacob Levy, Tyler Westenbroek, David Fridovich-Keil. Traditionally, model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) methods exploit neural networks as flexible function approximators to represent a priori unknown environment dynamics. However, training data are typically scarce in practice, and these black-box models often fail to generalize. Modeling architectures that leverage known physics can substantially reduce the complexity of system-identification, but break down in the face of complex phenomena such as contact.

arxiv-2503-22033.title: Radiative stabilization of the indenyl cation: Recurrent fluorescence in a closed-shell polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon
arxiv-2503-22033.creator: James N. Bull, Arun Subramani, Chang Liu, Samuel J. P. Marlton, Eleanor K. Ashworth, Henrik Cederquist, Henning Zettergren, Mark H. Stockett

arxiv-2510-07142.title: Slow, Fast and Opportunistic FAMA: A Spatial Block-Correlation Analysis under Nakagami- m m Fading Channels Thanks: P. R. de Moura is with the Electrical Engineering Department, University of Brasília, Brasília 70910-900, Brazil, and also with the Technical Advisory Unit, National Telecommunications
arxiv-2510-07142.creator: Paulo R. de Moura, Hugerles S. Silva
arxiv-2510-07142.description: Abstract This paper studies slow, fast and opportunistic fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA) under the effect of Nakagami- m m fading channels, considering the new and realistic spatial block-correlation model. Expressions for the outage probability (OP), based on the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR), are derived for slow FAMA.

pmc-12618647.title: Analysis of the role of water condition on the friction performance of calcareous sand from the nano-scale
pmc-12618647.creator: Kamal Al-Zaoari, Sha Lai, Wei-Qiang Feng
pmc-12618647.description: The strength of calcareous sand, which is closely related to the coastal stability, is controlled by the interparticle frictions. Therefore, it is essential to evaluate the friction behavior of soil particles under different water conditions to predict their potential failure.

pmc-12785790.title: Diagnostic Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Predicting Malignant Upgrade of B3 Breast Lesions: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12785790.creator: Romuald Ferre, Cherie M. Kuzmiak
pmc-12785790.description: Background/Objectives: High-risk (B3) breast lesions are a heterogeneous group with uncertain malignant potential. Methods: We systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed the ability of artificial-intelligence (AI) models to predict malignant upgrades (a ductal carcinoma in situ or an invasive carcinoma) after biopsy.

pmc-12819769.title: The association between interoception and psychopathic traits
pmc-12819769.creator: Yu Gao, Amanda Murphy, Liat Kofler
pmc-12819769.description: IntroductionPsychopathic traits are characterized by pervasive emotional deficits, including diminished empathy and remorse, heightened impulsivity, and antisocial behavior. Prior work has suggested that these traits may be partly shaped by physiological abnormality, although their associations with interoception—defined as the sensitivity to and awareness of internal bodily signals—has been inconsistent and understudied.

pmc-13003107.title: Neural predictors of treatment outcome through emotion regulation in internalizing disorders: a narrative review
pmc-13003107.creator: Heide Klumpp, Delaney Davey, Scott A. Langenecker
pmc-13003107.description: Internalizing disorders such as depressive and anxiety disorders are prevalent, disabling, and characterized by difficulty managing emotions particularly in the context of negative information. Despite the availability of empirically supported treatments, response to these treatments remains heterogeneous. Accruing data indicate neural predictors of treatment response have the potential to contribute to precision medicine to improve treatment outcomes.

pmc-13138010.title: High-fidelity bidirectional translation between single-cell transcriptomes and DNA methylomes with scBOND
pmc-13138010.creator: Kehan Lang, Chenyang Jia, Siyu Li, Yi Guo, Dingjun Hu, Shengquan Chen
pmc-13138010.description: Single-cell multiomic sequencing technologies have offered unprecedented insights into cellular heterogeneity by jointly profiling gene expression and epigenetic landscapes at single-cell resolution. However, the application of these technologies remains limited owing to technical challenges and high costs. Computational approaches for cross-modality translation provide a promising solution to these limitations by enabling the inference of one modality from another.

pmc-13395673.title: Glycemic and lipid responses to selenium-enriched vs. zeaxanthin-enriched eggs in patients with type 2 diabetes: a 12-week randomized controlled trial
pmc-13395673.creator: Xiaokang Niu, Yong Zhang, Yinghua Liu, Yinhua Zhu, Bing Fang, Chenghao Hu, Xiaojuan Xu, Ran Wang, Yue Sang, Qi Zhang, Jie Guo

pmc-13398555.title: Urinary DKK3 as a predictor of CKD stages in reflux nephropathy in children
pmc-13398555.creator: Ayşe Seda PINARBAŞI, Neslihan GÜNAY, İnayet GÜNTÜRK, Didem BARLAK KETI, Sibel YEL, Sekure Rabia ULUEREN, Cevat YAZICI, Hakan M. POYRAZOĞLU, İsmail DURSUN
pmc-13398555.description: Background/aimReflux nephropathy is an important cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children. The search for new biomarkers continues, as early intervention is important to slow the progression of CKD. Urinary Dickkopf-3 (uDKK3), a potential marker of tubulointerstitial fibrosis, has been studied in adults but not extensively in children with CKD.

pmc-13640315.title: Bioinformatics analysis of the sodium-dependent neurotransmitter transporter family in Bursaphelenchus xylophilus
pmc-13640315.creator: Caijin He, Shichao Wang, Haixiang Li, Na Pu, Wangyang Liao, Jie Chen, Xin Hao
